h3: 5.3 Outputs can be wrong, and agents act

p: AI makes mistakes. An Output can be inaccurate, out of date, biased, insecure or invented, including citations that do not exist. Code it writes can carry vulnerabilities or incompatible licences. Agents and connectors can take consequential Actions: they can change files, run code, reach other services and send messages. Give them the least access they need, keep backups, supervise actions that matter, and check results before you rely on them. The Services are not a substitute for a licensed professional.

We use your Materials to provide, secure, support and improve the Services and to meet legal obligations. Whether we also use your chats and coding sessions to train Zen models and other Hanzo systems is your choice:

li: You set it. The setting is “Help improve Hanzo’s models.” We show it to you before your first chat, and you can change it any time in Settings → Privacy. Agreeing to these Terms does not turn it on.
When it is on, we may use your chats and coding sessions, including their Inputs and Outputs, to train and evaluate Zen models and other Hanzo systems.
When it is off, we do not use new chats or coding sessions for that purpose. Turning it off does not reach back into training that has already begun, as the help page explains.

Two exceptions. Content our systems flag for safety or abuse may be reviewed and kept for that purpose, and — when the setting is off — it is not used for general training. Feedback you send (a rating, a report) may be used to improve the Services; a rating does not by itself authorize training on the whole conversation.

h2: 7. Benchmarks, research and the Verified Commons

p: The Services may run models against public, licensed, synthetic, or customer-provided benchmark items. You authorize Hanzo to execute, cache, reproduce, store, analyze, compare, and retain standardized evaluation records generated through the Services, including:

li: benchmark, dataset, task, and item identifiers;
benchmark prompts and reference answers where Hanzo has the necessary rights;
model, provider, endpoint, version, and date;
system and user prompts, templates, tool definitions, and workflow topology where permitted;
raw and normalized Outputs, candidate responses, reasoning or tool traces where collection is enabled and lawful;
correctness, judge, verifier, recovery, damage, disagreement, co-failure, safety, and fault labels;
seeds, sampling and decoding settings, retries, timeouts, and execution environment;
token usage, monetary cost, latency, throughput, cache status, and reliability; and
cryptographic hashes, provenance, consent, license, and reproducibility metadata.

p: These records are “Benchmark Records.” As between you and Hanzo and to the extent protectable under applicable law, Hanzo owns its compilation, normalization, measurement methodology, aggregate analyses, and Benchmark Records generated by Hanzo, excluding rights that you or a third party retain in underlying prompts, datasets, Inputs, facts, or model Outputs. Hanzo may retain nonpersonal Benchmark Records and provenance for the life of the registry or research program, including to avoid paying for duplicate runs, reproduce or dispute performance claims, detect model drift, train evaluation systems where permitted, and maintain longitudinal model histories. Personal data embedded in a Benchmark Record remains subject to the Privacy Policy, DPA, consent state, and applicable deletion rights.

Customer-provided benchmark content remains Customer Content and is private by default. Customer may separately authorize publication of identified results or contribution of a dataset. If you ask Hanzo to evaluate a private model, endpoint, dataset, or benchmark, you represent that you have authority to permit the evaluation and the requested level of storage and disclosure.

Subject to provider terms, benchmark licenses, confidentiality obligations, and applicable law, Hanzo may publish comparative scores, leaderboards, methodology, aggregate statistics, faults, replication results, and sufficient provenance to make results reproducible. Hanzo will not publish confidential prompts, private model Outputs, hidden test items, or Customer identity without authority.

User acceptance of these Terms does not create rights that a model provider or benchmark owner has not granted. Hanzo will maintain a Benchmark Rights Registry recording applicable dataset licenses, provider restrictions, publication permissions, attribution requirements, and embargoes. A result may be kept private, redacted, delayed, or removed when the necessary rights are absent or disputed.

Benchmark results describe the specific protocol, model version, date, sample, and environment tested. They are not guarantees of future performance. Hanzo may correct, qualify, or withdraw results when protocols, provider behavior, contamination, faults, or measurement errors are discovered.

Private research participation does not authorize public release. Publication to the Hanzo Verified Commons, Hugging Face, or another public repository requires a separate contribution action specifying the data and license. Public release may be difficult or impossible to retract from third-party copies; the contribution flow will explain this before publication.
